chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
One dirham of interest (usury) is more grievous than seventy adulteries, all of which are with those of close kin (incestuous).
ai.seo_question: How does the severity of one dirham of usury compare to adultery in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) states that a single dirham of usury (riba) is more severe than seventy acts of adultery, specifically those committed with close relatives. This comparison underscores the unique spiritual gravity of riba, which is often viewed as a war against God and His Messenger, distinguishing it from other major sins. The emphasis on 'close relatives' (dhawil mahram) highlights the compounding nature of the sin, linking financial corruption with familial and social disintegration.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, form Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘One Dirham of interest is more grievous than seventy adulteries, all of these being with the ones with sanctity (incestuous)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim, who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The sin of receiving one dirham of Riba ’ (unlawful interest) is more serious than having carnal relations with one’s relatives (with whom marriage is unlawful).”
